subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a parent-self-only delegate tool policy for orchestrator agents, and if yes what syntax and audit semantics should become the public config contract?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but allowing a child session to receive command/file tools that the parent model cannot use directly changes the authorization boundary and cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Add explicit delegate-only policy
options.body: Define one canonical config surface, keep `deny` absolute, remove delegate-only tools from the parent model surface, and persist/audit child access with focused tests and docs.

options.title: Keep non-escalating policy only
options.body: Reject delegate-only semantics for now and document separate worker-agent IDs or existing subagent policy as the supported pattern.

options.title: Defer to broader tool-policy redesign
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers design a broader per-spawn/per-agent tool contract that also covers related schema and least-privilege requests.

recommendation.title: Add explicit delegate-only policy
recommendation.body: Define one canonical config surface, keep `deny` absolute, remove delegate-only tools from the parent model surface, and persist/audit child access with focused tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue needs product/security direction more than a mechanical code owner, and the related review history routes this decision to steipete as the strongest available follow-up owner signal.
